mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 units, sustained for 2 months, indicates strengthening demand, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and GDP growth
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or HOUST-GDP growth correlation breaks down (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 6.5% and the payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth rate exceeds 1.5% over 3 months, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 6.5% and PAYEMS growth > 1.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or labor market indicators diverge (UNRATE rises while PAYEMS growth slows).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, coupled with a rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above its 3-month moving average, signals supply chain disruptions and potential inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 55% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or supply chain-industrial production correlation breaks down (p-value > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, sustained for 2 quarters, indicates increased consumer spending power, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 45% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or consumer spending power-RSAFS correlation weakens (p-value > 0.12).

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 4.5% for 2 consecutive months signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical interest rate impacts on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or FEDFUNDS-equity market correlation breaks down (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth rate slows down below 1% over 2 consecutive quarters, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 55% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or labor market indicators diverge (UNRATE falls while PAYEMS growth slows).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP (GDPC1) above its 4-quarter moving average, coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 7%, signals strong economic growth and low unemployment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP-unemployment impacts on equity markets
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or GDP-unemployment correlation breaks down (p-value > 0.15).
